\mathbb C$ of a formal power series or of an analytic function at $0$. Set
$c_k=0$ for negative $k$. Seek a normalized denominator
$q(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^nq_jz^j$. Form the $n\times n$ moment system
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n}q_jc_{m+\ell-j}=-c_{m+\ell}, \qquad 1\le\ell\le n.$$
Classify it by exact Gaussian elimination on the augmented matrix. Start with
pivot row $r=1$ and scan columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ in order. In column $j$, if
all entries in rows $r$ through $n$ are zero, leave that column free and
continue. Otherwise choose the first row $s\ge r$ with a nonzero entry in
column $j$, swap rows $s$ and $r$, divide row $r$ by its column-$j$ entry,
and subtract the resulting row multiple from every other row to make the
other entries in column $j$ zero; then increment $r$. After all columns, a
row whose coefficient entries are all zero and whose augmented entry is
nonzero makes the system inconsistent, so return status
$\texttt{full-order-inconsistent}$. If the system is consistent but has
rank less than $n$, return status $\texttt{defective-nonunique}$ together
with the rank and reduced system; do not select a denominator from its
affine solution set. Here rank is the number of pivot rows; consistency and rank are
read from the reduced augmented matrix. If the system has rank $n$, return the unique solution
$(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$ and set
$$p_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,n)}q_jc_{k-j}, \qquad 0\le k\le m,\qquad q_0:=1.$$
The output is the coefficient-matching candidate $p/q$ with its full-order
status. If $n=0$, the empty denominator system is uniquely solved by $q=1$
and the returned numerator coefficients are $p_k=c_k$ for $0\le k\le m$.
This procedure claims no pole-location or analytic-continuation guarantee.

$Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\subset\mathbb C$, data
$F=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\in\mathbb C^N$, an absolute tolerance $\tau\ge0$, an
integer support budget $B$ with $0\le B\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, and a finite
bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $S\ge0$. The procedure is evaluated in exact
arithmetic; its finite-precision implementation makes no optimality claim.
For $v\in\mathbb C^k$, use the standard Hermitian inner product and Euclidean
norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^k|v_j|^2)^{1/2}$.

1. Set the initial rational candidate $r_0$ to the constant mean
$\bar f=N^{-1}\sum_i f_i$. Compute
$\eta_0=\max_i|f_i-\bar f|$. If $\eta_0\le\tau$, return
$(r_0,\varnothing,\texttt{tolerance-met})$.

2. For $m=1,\ldots,B$, choose the least original index among the remaining
sample points that maximizes the absolute residual from the last accepted
rational candidate. Append that point and its datum provisionally to the
support list; remove it from the remaining sample list.

3. Form the $(N-m)\times m$ Loewner matrix
$L_{ij}=(f_i-f_{s_j})/(z_i-z_{s_j})$, where $i$ ranges over the remaining
sample indices and $s_j$ are the provisional support indices. The denominator
is nonzero because all sample points are distinct.

4. Compute an exact full singular value decomposition (SVD) of $L$ by applying
[[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] followed by
[[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]] with zero deflation
tolerance and budget $S$. If either call returns failure or the QR budget is
exhausted, return the last accepted candidate and status
$\texttt{inconclusive}$.

5. Let $E$ be the right singular subspace for the smallest singular value of
$L$, and let $P_E$ be its orthogonal projection. Choose the least coordinate
index $j$ for which $P_Ee_j\ne0$ and set $w=P_Ee_j/\|P_Ee_j\|_2$. This rule
applies at every multiplicity, including dimension one. Multiply by the
unique unit scalar that makes the first nonzero coordinate of $w$ positive
real. If any coordinate of $w$ is zero, reject this provisional support and
return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{zero-support-weight}$.

nodes, their data, and $w$ as its weights. If this rational function has a
genuine pole at any remaining sample point, reject this provisional support
and return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{pole-status}$.
Otherwise accept the candidate and record both its maximum sampled residual
$\eta_m$ and the Loewner residual $\sigma_m=\|Lw\|_2$. If
$\eta_m\le\tau$, return status $\texttt{tolerance-met}$.

accepted candidate with status $\texttt{support-budget-exhausted}$. In
particular $B=0$ returns the initial constant with this status when step 1
does not return.

deterministic, including when the smallest singular value has multiplicity

Input nonnegative integers $m,n$ and coefficients $c_0,\ldots,c_{m+n}\in
\mathbb C$ of a formal power series or of an analytic function at $0$. Set
$c_k=0$ for negative $k$. Seek a normalized denominator
$q(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^nq_jz^j$. Form the $n\times n$ moment system
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n}q_jc_{m+\ell-j}=-c_{m+\ell}, \qquad 1\le\ell\le n.$$
Classify it by exact Gaussian elimination on the augmented matrix. Start with
pivot row $r=1$ and scan columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ in order. In column $j$, if
all entries in rows $r$ through $n$ are zero, leave that column free and
continue. Otherwise choose the first row $s\ge r$ with a nonzero entry in
column $j$, swap rows $s$ and $r$, divide row $r$ by its column-$j$ entry,
and subtract the resulting row multiple from every other row to make the
other entries in column $j$ zero; then increment $r$. After all columns, a
row whose coefficient entries are all zero and whose augmented entry is
nonzero makes the system inconsistent, so return status
$\texttt{full-order-inconsistent}$. If the system is consistent but has
rank less than $n$, return status $\texttt{defective-nonunique}$ together
with the rank and reduced system; do not select a denominator from its
affine solution set. Here rank is the number of pivot rows; consistency and rank are
read from the reduced augmented matrix. If the system has rank $n$, return the unique solution
$(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$ and set
$$p_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,n)}q_jc_{k-j}, \qquad 0\le k\le m,\qquad q_0:=1.$$
The output is the coefficient-matching candidate $p/q$ with its full-order
status. If $n=0$, the empty denominator system is uniquely solved by $q=1$
and the returned numerator coefficients are $p_k=c_k$ for $0\le k\le m$.
This procedure claims no pole-location or analytic-continuation guarantee.

Let $m,n\ge0$, $R>0$, and
$f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty c_kz^k$ for $|z|<R$, with the series convergent
there. Suppose $q_0=1,q_1,\ldots,q_n$ solve the full normalized
Padé moment equations of [[alg-pade-coefficient-matching]]. Define
$p_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,n)}q_jc_{k-j}$ for $0\le k\le m$, and
$p(z)=\sum_{k=0}^mp_kz^k$, $q(z)=\sum_{j=0}^nq_jz^j$. Then
$$
f(z)-\frac{p(z)}{q(z)}=O(z^{m+n+1})\quad\text{as }z\to0.
$$
This is a local Taylor-matching statement only; it gives no pole-location
claim and no guarantee about analytic continuation beyond the neighborhood
where $f$ is given.

Here $h(z)=O(z^M)$ as $z\to0$ means there are constants $C,\delta>0$ such
that $|h(z)|\le C|z|^M$ whenever $0<|z|<\delta$.

Input a nonempty ordered list of distinct sample points
$Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\subset\mathbb C$, data
$F=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\in\mathbb C^N$, an absolute tolerance $\tau\ge0$, an
integer support budget $B$ with $0\le B\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, and a finite
bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $S\ge0$. The procedure is evaluated in exact
arithmetic; its finite-precision implementation makes no optimality claim.
For $v\in\mathbb C^k$, use the standard Hermitian inner product and Euclidean
norm $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^k|v_j|^2)^{1/2}$.

1. Set the initial rational candidate $r_0$ to the constant mean
$\bar f=N^{-1}\sum_i f_i$. Compute
$\eta_0=\max_i|f_i-\bar f|$. If $\eta_0\le\tau$, return
$(r_0,\varnothing,\texttt{tolerance-met})$.

2. For $m=1,\ldots,B$, choose the least original index among the remaining
sample points that maximizes the absolute residual from the last accepted
rational candidate. Append that point and its datum provisionally to the
support list; remove it from the remaining sample list.

3. Form the $(N-m)\times m$ Loewner matrix
$L_{ij}=(f_i-f_{s_j})/(z_i-z_{s_j})$, where $i$ ranges over the remaining
sample indices and $s_j$ are the provisional support indices. The denominator
is nonzero because all sample points are distinct.

4. Compute an exact full singular value decomposition (SVD) of $L$ by applying
[[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] followed by
[[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]] with zero deflation
tolerance and budget $S$. If either call returns failure or the QR budget is
exhausted, return the last accepted candidate and status
$\texttt{inconclusive}$.

5. Let $E$ be the right singular subspace for the smallest singular value of
$L$, and let $P_E$ be its orthogonal projection. Choose the least coordinate
index $j$ for which $P_Ee_j\ne0$ and set $w=P_Ee_j/\|P_Ee_j\|_2$. This rule
applies at every multiplicity, including dimension one. Multiply by the
unique unit scalar that makes the first nonzero coordinate of $w$ positive
real. If any coordinate of $w$ is zero, reject this provisional support and
return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{zero-support-weight}$.

6. Form the barycentric rational quotient using the provisional support
nodes, their data, and $w$ as its weights. If this rational function has a
genuine pole at any remaining sample point, reject this provisional support
and return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{pole-status}$.
Otherwise accept the candidate and record both its maximum sampled residual
$\eta_m$ and the Loewner residual $\sigma_m=\|Lw\|_2$. If
$\eta_m\le\tau$, return status $\texttt{tolerance-met}$.

7. If all $B$ iterations finish without another return, return the last
accepted candidate with status $\texttt{support-budget-exhausted}$. In
particular $B=0$ returns the initial constant with this status when step 1
does not return.

The support tie rule and the projection rule make the exact procedure
deterministic, including when the smallest singular value has multiplicity
greater than one. Rank deficiency is permitted: if the smallest singular
value is zero and all selected weights are nonzero and the quotient is finite
at the remaining sample points, the candidate is accepted and its exact
sample residual is evaluated. The algorithm asserts no uniform off-grid error
bound and no minimax optimality. The Loewner residual $\sigma_m$ is a linear
least-squares residual, not the nonlinear sampled residual $\eta_m$.

$\eta_0=\max_i|f_i-\bar f|$. If $\eta_0\le\tau$, return
$(r_0,\varnothing,\texttt{tolerance-met})$.

2. For $m=1,\ldots,B$, choose the least original index among the remaining
sample points that maximizes the absolute residual from the last accepted
rational candidate. Append that point and its datum provisionally to the
support list; remove it from the remaining sample list.

3. Form the $(N-m)\times m$ Loewner matrix
$L_{ij}=(f_i-f_{s_j})/(z_i-z_{s_j})$, where $i$ ranges over the remaining
sample indices and $s_j$ are the provisional support indices. The denominator
is nonzero because all sample points are distinct.

4. Compute an exact full singular value decomposition (SVD) of $L$ by applying
[[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] followed by
[[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]] with zero deflation
tolerance and budget $S$. If either call returns failure or the QR budget is
exhausted, return the last accepted candidate and status
$\texttt{inconclusive}$.

5. Let $E$ be the right singular subspace for the smallest singular value of
$L$, and let $P_E$ be its orthogonal projection. Choose the least coordinate
index $j$ for which $P_Ee_j\ne0$ and set $w=P_Ee_j/\|P_Ee_j\|_2$. This rule
applies at every multiplicity, including dimension one. Multiply by the
unique unit scalar that makes the first nonzero coordinate of $w$ positive
real. If any coordinate of $w$ is zero, reject this provisional support and
return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{zero-support-weight}$.

6. Form the barycentric rational quotient using the provisional support
nodes, their data, and $w$ as its weights. If this rational function has a
genuine pole at any remaining sample point, reject this provisional support
and return the last accepted candidate with status $\texttt{pole-status}$.
Otherwise accept the candidate and record both its maximum sampled residual
$\eta_m$ and the Loewner residual $\sigma_m=\|Lw\|_2$. If
$\eta_m\le\tau$, return status $\texttt{tolerance-met}$.

7. If all $B$ iterations finish without another return, return the last
accepted candidate with status $\texttt{support-budget-exhausted}$. In
particular $B=0$ returns the initial constant with this status when step 1
does not return.

The support tie rule and the projection rule make the exact procedure
deterministic, including when the smallest singular value has multiplicity
greater than one. Rank deficiency is permitted: if the smallest singular
value is zero and all selected weights are nonzero and the quotient is finite
at the remaining sample points, the candidate is accepted and its exact
sample residual is evaluated. The algorithm asserts no uniform off-grid error
bound and no minimax optimality. The Loewner residual $\sigma_m$ is a linear
least-squares residual, not the nonlinear sampled residual $\eta_m$.

At an AAA iteration with Loewner matrix $L\in\mathbb C^{(N-m)\times m}$,
the selected unit weight vector $w$ minimizes $\|Lv\|_2$ among all
$v\in\mathbb C^m$ with $\|v\|_2=1$; its residual is the smallest singular
value of $L$. If every selected weight is nonzero and the iteration does not
return pole status, its barycentric candidate interpolates all selected
support data. The finite support budget makes the procedure terminate after
at most $B$ iterations. These claims concern finite sampled data and do not
assert minimax optimality or uniform off-grid convergence.

Let $k\ge1$, let $z_1,\ldots,z_k\in\mathbb C$ be distinct support nodes, let
$f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathbb C$ be data, and let each weight $w_j\in\mathbb C$ be
nonzero. Define the cleared polynomials
$$P(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_jf_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell), \qquad Q(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell).$$
The **barycentric rational quotient** is the rational function $r=P/Q$.
Away from the support nodes this equals
$$r(z)= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_jf_j/(z-z_j)} {\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_j/(z-z_j)}.$$
At a support node its value is given by the cleared quotient $P(z_j)/Q(z_j)$.
A **pole** means a zero of the denominator after all common polynomial
factors of numerator and denominator have been canceled.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, where $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Put $p=\min(m,n)$ and $M=\max(m,n)$. If $m\ge n$, set $C=A$; if $m<n$, set $C=A^*$. Thus $C\in\mathbb F^{M\times p}$.

Save the input as $C_0=C$ and initialize $U=I_M$, $V=I_p$, and empty ordered lists of stored local left and right transformations. For $k=1,\ldots,p$, in this order:

1. Let $x=C_{k:M,k}$. If $x=0$, use the identity left transformation. Otherwise choose $\phi=x_1/|x_1|$ when $x_1\ne0$ and $\phi=1$ when $x_1=0$, set $\alpha=-\phi\|x\|_2$, $v=x-\alpha e_1$, and $h=v/\|v\|_2$. Use the Householder reflector $H=I-2hh^*$ on rows $k:M$. Update $C\leftarrow H^*C$ on those rows and append this local transformation to the left list. In exact arithmetic update $U\leftarrow U\operatorname{diag}(I_{k-1},H)$. In finite precision update columns $k:M$ of the dense accumulator $U$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $U$.
2. If $k<p$, let $y=C_{k,k+1:p}^*$. If $y=0$, use the identity right transformation. Otherwise apply the same phase and normalization rule to $y$ to form the Householder reflector $G$, then apply $C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$ and append this local transformation to the right list. In exact arithmetic update $V\leftarrow V\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$. In finite precision update columns $k+1:p$ of the dense accumulator $V$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $V$.

Set $B$ to the leading $p\times p$ block of the final work matrix $C$, and return $B,U,V$ together with the ordered local transformation lists.

In finite precision, each left/right reflector uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], including its real/complex scaled formation, range checks and exact target-column/row zero writes. This is the arithmetic realization of the exact steps above. A zero active vector takes the identity branch. Any helper `range-failure`, invalid operation, nonfinite value, or nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range returns `range-failure` with the partial factors and stored local transformations; otherwise return `success`, $B,U,V$, the ordered stored local transformations, the reconstruction residual $\|C_0-U\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}V^*\|_F$, and the two orthogonality residuals $\|U^*U-I\|_F$ and $\|V^*V-I\|_F$. The reconstruction uses the saved input $C_0$, not the overwritten work matrix. The exact products of the stored unitary representatives are the theoretical factors; the dense finite-precision accumulators are rounded and their residuals are computed quantities, not certified bounds by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]].

Input the original $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, the successful output record of [[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] for $C=A$ if $m\ge n$ and $C=A^*$ otherwise, a deflation tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and a finite nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$. The reduction record supplies the upper bidiagonal work matrix $B_0$, dense accumulators $U_B,V_B$, and ordered stored local transformation data. Initialize $B=B_0$, the sweep accumulators $U_\Sigma,V_\Sigma$ to identities of order $p=\min(m,n)$, empty ordered left/right transformation lists, an empty deflation record, a pass counter $t=0$, and a sweep counter $s=0$. Write the diagonal as $d_i$ and superdiagonal as $e_i$, and set $e_0=0$.

At the start of each pass, set $t\leftarrow t+1$, set $e_i$ to zero and append $(t,i,e_i^{old})$ to the deflation record whenever $|e_i|\le\tau(|d_i|+|d_{i+1}|)$. The corresponding additive matrix change has entry $-e_i^{old}$ at $(i,i+1)$ and zero elsewhere. Record any later non-target sparsity cleanup the same way with its row, column, and old value. The zero entries split the active blocks. If every active block has size one, stop with `converged`. Otherwise process the active blocks in increasing order of $\ell$, skipping singleton blocks. Before each block sweep, if $s=N$, stop with `budget-exhausted`; otherwise form only the tridiagonal entries of $T=B^*B$ on that block: $T_{ii}=|d_i|^2+|e_{i-1}|^2$ and $T_{i,i+1}=\overline{d_i}e_i$. Choose $\mu$ to be the eigenvalue of the trailing Hermitian block $\begin{bmatrix}T_{r-1,r-1}&T_{r-1,r}\\T_{r,r-1}&T_{rr}\end{bmatrix}$ closest to $T_{rr}$, resolving a tie by the smaller eigenvalue. If the leading pivot $d_\ell$ is zero or has magnitude at most $\tau\max(|e_{\ell-1}|,|e_\ell|)$, use the zero-shift branch $\mu=0$ and choose the initial right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $(d_\ell,e_\ell)G_\ell=(\rho,0)$, avoiding division by the small or zero diagonal.

**Finite-precision shift and comparison schedule.** The preceding exact-arithmetic formulas retain their exact meaning. For finite precision use the scalar order, six-real-operation complex product, scaled real-component norm, and first-failing-primitive range policy of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] also for the following stages. All assignments below are stored; do not fuse operations. Comparisons, maxima, copies, conjugations, sign changes, and real absolute values are exact operations on stored finite values. Evaluate each complex magnitude by that helper's scaled two-component norm, with zero magnitude returned exactly as zero. At each pass visit deflation indices increasingly; at index $i$ evaluate $a_i=|e_i|$, $b_i=|d_i|$, $c_i=|d_{i+1}|$ in that order, then $h_i=\operatorname{fl}(b_i+c_i)$ and $k_i=\operatorname{fl}(\tau h_i)$, and deflate exactly when $a_i\le k_i$.

For each nonsingleton block, form its Gram diagonal entries in increasing index order, followed by its upper off-diagonal entries in increasing index order. To form $T_{ii}$, square $\Re d_i,\Im d_i,\Re e_{i-1},\Im e_{i-1}$ separately with rounding, add the first two rounded squares, add the last two, and add these two rounded sums, rounding each addition. Form $T_{i,i+1}$ by the helper's complex product for $\overline{d_i}e_i$ and copy its conjugate to the lower off-diagonal. No other Gram entries are formed. Write the stored trailing block as $\begin{bmatrix}a&z\\\overline z&c\end{bmatrix}$. In this order compute $h=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a+c)/2)$, $\delta=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a-c)/2)$, and $k$ by the helper's scaled norm on the ordered four-real-component list $(\delta,0,\Re z,\Im z)$, corresponding to the complex vector $(\delta,z)$, returning exact zero for the zero list. Then compute $\mu_-=\operatorname{fl}(h-k)$, $\mu_+=\operatorname{fl}(h+k)$, $q_-=|\operatorname{fl}(\mu_--c)|$, and $q_+=|\operatorname{fl}(\mu_+-c)|$. Choose $\mu=\mu_-$ if $q_-\le q_+$ and $\mu=\mu_+$ otherwise. In exact arithmetic these are the two Hermitian eigenvalues and the stated nearest-eigenvalue/tie rule; in finite precision they specify the shift estimates without asserting their accuracy.

Next evaluate $|d_\ell|$, $|e_{\ell-1}|$, and $|e_\ell|$ in that order and form $w=\operatorname{fl}(\tau\max(|e_{\ell-1}|,|e_\ell|))$. Use the zero-shift branch exactly when $d_\ell=0$ or $|d_\ell|\le w$. In the ordinary branch form the first shift-vector entry as $\operatorname{fl}(T_{\ell\ell}-\mu)$ and use the stored lower Gram entry as its second entry. If any of these primitives fails the helper's normal-range/finite-value requirements, return the existing `range-failure` record immediately, before any sweep transformation for that block. This rule permits range failure in shift formation and makes no unconditional progress claim. For $p=0$ or only singleton active blocks none of the block stages is requested.

In the ordinary branch choose the first right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $G_\ell^*(T_{\ell\ell}-\mu,T_{\ell+1,\ell})^T=(\rho,0)^T$, where $T_{\ell+1,\ell}=\overline{e_\ell}d_\ell$. In either branch, apply $B\leftarrow BG_\ell$, update columns $\ell,\ell+1$ of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. For $j=\ell,\ldots,r-1$, choose a left Givens factor $H_j$ so that $H_j^*(B_{j,j},B_{j+1,j})^T=(\rho,0)^T$; apply it to rows $j,j+1$, update columns $j,j+1$ of $U_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the left list. If $j<r-1$, choose a right Givens factor $G_{j+1}$ so that $(B_{j,j+1},B_{j,j+2})G_{j+1}=(\rho,0)$; apply it to columns $j+1,j+2$, update the corresponding columns of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. Continue until the bulge reaches the active block endpoint. A zero annihilation vector uses the identity rotation. In finite precision each Givens formation/update uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], conjugate-transposed as needed for the stated left/right orientation; accumulator multiplications use the same stored local data but omit all target-zero writes. The dense accumulator multiplications follow the operationwise arithmetic model, while the ordered lists retain the exact unitary representatives used in analysis. Target zero writes to $B$ are included in their local error bounds. The initial shift-vector rotation does not zero an unrelated entry of $B$. Each Givens factor is chosen using [[def-real-and-complex-givens-transformations]] and its annihilation guarantee in [[thm-householder-reflectors-and-givens-transformations-are-unitary-and-annihilate-targeted-entries]].

After each processed block, increment $s$ by one. Once all current active blocks have been processed, start a new pass. If any operation, norm or pivot is invalid or nonfinite, or a nonzero exact intermediate is outside the normal range, return `range-failure` with the partial $B$, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, and available residual reports. On `budget-exhausted`, return the current $B$, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, triplet residuals, and orthogonality residuals. On `converged`, set $B_{\mathrm{final}}=B$ and return it with both dense accumulators, both transformation lists, the deflation record, triplet/orthogonality residuals, and its tall embedding $\overline B_{\mathrm{final}}=\begin{bmatrix}B_{\mathrm{final}}\\0_{M-p,p}\end{bmatrix}$.

For every exit other than `range-failure`, let $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the current work matrix, and let $d_i=(B_{\mathrm{out}})_{ii}$. Obtain each candidate value as $\widehat\sigma_i=|d_i|$ by the scaled two-component modulus evaluation (real absolute value is exact). On `converged`, the active-block condition makes $B_{\mathrm{out}}=B_{\mathrm{final}}$ diagonal; after `budget-exhausted`, the diagonal values are estimates only and carry no accuracy claim.

Let $W_B=\operatorname{diag}(U_\Sigma,I_{M-p})$. In exact arithmetic the tall-orientation accumulated factors are $U_C=U_BW_B$ and $V_C=V_BV_\Sigma$. In finite precision form each dense product by row-by-column multiplication, with six-real-operation complex products and sequential componentwise rounded additions under the operationwise model; return `range-failure` if any required intermediate is invalid, nonfinite, or outside the normal range. Their exact theoretical factors are the products represented by the ordered local transformation lists together with the bidiagonal-reduction lists. If $m\ge n$, set $\widehat U=U_C$ and $\widehat V=V_C$; for each nonzero $d_i$, multiply column $i$ of $\widehat U$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ in exact arithmetic, using componentwise division by the successful scaled modulus readout in finite precision. If $m<n$, set $\widehat U=V_C$ and $\widehat V=U_C$; in this wide orientation multiply column $i$ of $\widehat V$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ instead. Sort the candidate values in nonincreasing order, breaking ties by their original diagonal index, and permute the corresponding columns of the returned triplet vectors in the same way; leave $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ and the transformation lists in their algorithmic order. For every candidate triplet $(\widehat\sigma_i,\widehat u_i,\widehat v_i)$, report $\|A\widehat v_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat u_i\|_2$ and $\|A^*\widehat u_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat v_i\|_2$. Also report $\|\widehat U^*\widehat U-I\|_F$ and $\|\widehat V^*\widehat V-I\|_F$. The reports expose finite-budget and rounding behavior; they do not certify convergence by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. Any additional sparsity cleanup is recorded separately in the deflation record with its discarded-entry perturbation.

Let $n\ge 2$ and let $0\le i<j\le n-1$.

A **real Givens rotation** in the $(i,j)$-plane is the identity matrix except on
rows and columns $i,j$, where it has the $2\times 2$ block

$$\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-s&c\end{pmatrix}\qquad(c,s\in\mathbb R,\ c^2+s^2=1).$$A **complex Givens transformation** in the $(i,j)$-plane is the identity except on rows and columns $i,j$, where it has block$$\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-\overline s&c\end{pmatrix},$$

with $c\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}$, $s\in\mathbb C$, and $c^2+|s|^2=1$. The modulus
$|s|$ is the one from [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]].

Such transformations act only on the two chosen coordinates and are designed to
zero one targeted entry while preserving the Euclidean norm from
[[def-inner-product-norm]].

For $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, the exact-arithmetic algorithm [[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] returns unitary $U,V$ and an upper bidiagonal $B\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$, $p=\min(m,n)$, such that if $m\ge n$ then $U^*AV=\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}$, and if $m<n$ then $U^*A^*V=\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}$.

Their largest absolute residuals are tied at $z=1$ and $z=3$; [F1] selects the earlier sample $z=1$. The first Loewner matrix is the single column $(-1/2,1,1/2)^T$, since its entries are $$\frac{H(0)-H(1)}{0-1}=-\frac12,\qquad \frac{H(3)-H(1)}{3-1}=1,\qquad \frac{H(4)-H(1)}{4-1}=\frac12.$$ Since its right domain is one-dimensional, the selected unit weight is $1$ under the phase rule. Its Householder reduction has a single diagonal entry; by [F5] there is only a singleton block, so the SVD call converges without using a sweep. The one-support quotient is the constant $-1$. Its remaining residual magnitudes are $1/2,2,3/2$ at $z=0,3,4$, respectively, so $\eta_1=2>\tau$ and the second support is $z=3$.

The remaining sample points are $0$ and $4$. In that row and support order, the Loewner matrix is $$L=\begin{bmatrix}-1/2&1/2\\1/2&-1/2\end{bmatrix}.$$ The rows are negatives of one another and $L(1,1)^T=0$, so $L$ has rank one, its smallest singular value is zero, and its right nullspace is spanned by $(1,1)$. The orthogonal projection of $e_1$ onto this line is $(1/2,1/2)$; normalizing it and applying the positive-real phase rule [F1] gives $w=(1,1)/\sqrt2$, whose components are both nonzero.

Substitution into the barycentric quotient [F3] gives $$r(z)= \frac{-1/(z-1)+1/(z-3)}{1/(z-1)+1/(z-3)} =\frac1{z-2}.$$ The denominator reduces to a nonzero constant times $z-2$, so its sole finite pole is $2$. The values at $z=0,4$ are $-1/2,1/2$; the support values at $z=1,3$ are $-1,1$ by [F2]. Thus this quotient matches all four data.

At the second support addition the Loewner matrix in step 1.2 is $$L=\begin{bmatrix}-1/2&1/2\\1/2&-1/2\end{bmatrix}.$$ Its first column has norm $1/\sqrt2$ and its second is its negative. By [F4] and [F7], the left Householder sends the first column to $(1/\sqrt2,0)^T$ and the second to $(-1/\sqrt2,0)^T$. The one-dimensional right active scalar is $-1/\sqrt2$; its phase is $-1$, its reflector vector is $-1$, and its Householder factor is $[-1]$. Thus the bidiagonal reduction returns $$B_0=\begin{bmatrix}1/\sqrt2&1/\sqrt2\\0&0\end{bmatrix}.$$ Then $$B_0^*B_0=\begin{bmatrix}1/2&1/2\\1/2&1/2\end{bmatrix}.$$ Its eigenvalues are $0$ and $1$, each at distance $1/2$ from the trailing diagonal entry $1/2$, so [F5] chooses shift $0$. The initial shift vector is $(1/2,1/2)^T$. The real Givens factor $$G=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$$ satisfies $G^*(1/2,1/2)^T=(1/\sqrt2,0)^T$, and $B_0G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$. The left rotation is the identity because the subdiagonal entry is already zero. Thus one block sweep makes the superdiagonal zero; the next zero-tolerance pass deflates it and sees only singleton blocks before checking the exhausted budget, so the SVD call succeeds with $S=1$. Step 2.1 shows all four samples match, hence $\eta_2=0=\tau$ and [F1]'s tolerance branch returns the exact quotient.

Let $n\ge1$, let $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be distinct real nodes, let
$f_0,\ldots,f_n\in\mathbb R$ be data, and let $d$ be an integer with
$0\le d<n$. For $j=0,\ldots,n$, define
$$w_j=(-1)^{j-d} \sum_{i=\max(0,j-d)}^{\min(j,n-d)} \prod_{\substack{i\le k\le i+d\\k\ne j}}|x_j-x_k|^{-1}.$$
The index range is nonempty and every product is positive, so every $w_j$ is
nonzero. The **Floater–Hormann interpolant of degree parameter $d$** is the
barycentric rational quotient of these nodes, data, and weights from
[[def-barycentric-rational-quotient]]. Away from the nodes, exact evaluation
uses the quotient with this denominator;
a zero of the reduced denominator is reported as pole status. The no-real-pole
theorem below proves that this status never occurs for admissible exact real
inputs.

For any $n\ge1$, any distinct ordered real nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_n$, any real
data $f_0,\ldots,f_n$, and any integer $0\le d<n$, the exact
Floater–Hormann rational function in
[[def-floater-hormann-interpolant]] has no real poles.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and $f:I\to\mathbb R$. Put $f^{(0)}:=f$. Recursively, wherever $f^{(j)}$ is differentiable, put $f^{(j+1)}:=(f^{(j)})'$, with derivatives at endpoints understood in the one-sided sense fixed by [[def-derivative]] and [[def-one-sided-limits]].

For $k\in\mathbb N$, the function is **$k$-times differentiable** on $I$ if $f^{(j)}$ exists on $I$ for every $j\le k$. It is of class **$C^k$** on $I$ if these derivatives exist and every $f^{(j)}$, $0\le j\le k$, is continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]). It is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, if it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Since $0\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), $C^0$ means continuity. The definitions also give $C^{k+1}\subseteq C^k$. Existence of $f^{(k)}$ alone does not assert that $f^{(k)}$ is continuous.

Let $k\ge1$, let $z_1,\ldots,z_k\in\mathbb C$ be distinct support nodes, let
$f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathbb C$ be data, and let each weight $w_j\in\mathbb C$ be
nonzero. Define the cleared polynomials
$$P(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_jf_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell), \qquad Q(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_j\prod_{\ell\ne j}(z-z_\ell).$$
The **barycentric rational quotient** is the rational function $r=P/Q$.
Away from the support nodes this equals
$$r(z)= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_jf_j/(z-z_j)} {\sum_{j=1}^{k} w_j/(z-z_j)}.$$
At a support node its value is given by the cleared quotient $P(z_j)/Q(z_j)$.
A **pole** means a zero of the denominator after all common polynomial
factors of numerator and denominator have been canceled.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $A$
([[def-continuity-real]]) and let $K \subseteq A$ be **nonempty** and compact
([[def-open-cover-r]]). Then $\sup f[K]$ and $\inf f[K]$ exist and are
**attained**: there are $p, q \in K$ with

$$f(q) \;=\; \inf f[K] \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; \sup f[K] \;=\; f(p) \qquad \text{for every } x \in K .$$

Equivalently, the set $f[K]$ has a maximum and a minimum
([[def-max-min]]), namely $\max f[K] = f(p)$ and $\min f[K] = f(q)$.

**Nonemptiness of $K$ is a hypothesis, not an oversight.** For $K = \varnothing$
the set $f[K]$ is empty, and neither a supremum nor a maximum of the empty set
exists in this library ([[def-complete-ordered-field]] supplies suprema of
nonempty sets bounded above only).

**This theorem is stated twice in this library, on purpose.** Its metric-space
twin is [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], proved from the cover machinery of metric
spaces; the proof below is $\mathbb{R}$-native, running through Heine-Borel for
$\mathbb{R}$ and the order-completeness of $\mathbb{R}$, and it uses no cover
argument beyond the one already spent in
[[thm-continuous-image-of-a-compact-set-r]]. That the two statements are the
same statement in two vocabularies is proved in
[[lem-real-and-metric-notions-agree]], later on this page.

derivations.claim: Fix $d\ge0$. For every integer $n\ge2d+2$, take $h=1/n$, $x_j=jh$ on $[0,1]$, and query $x=h/2$. This family has $h/h_{\min}=1$. From [F1], after multiplying every weight by the same positive factor $h^dd!$, its weights are $$\widetilde w_j=(-1)^{j-d}\delta_j,\qquad \delta_j=\sum_{i=\max(0,j-d)}^{\min(j,n-d)}\binom d{j-i}.$$ Indeed, on a uniform mesh each reciprocal-distance product in [F1] equals $h^{-d}/((j-i)!(i+d-j)!)$. Thus $1\le\delta_j\le2^d$, and $\delta_j=2^d$ for $d\le j\le n-d$.
